To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
MS2 inactivation in natural waters can occur by an indirect mechanism involving 1O2 and that 1O2 is a significant contributor to inactivation in WSP waters.
the indirect mechanism is quantitatively more significant than direct damage by UV light for inactivation of MS 2 in WSP water.

(1) the indirect mechanism is important for the inactivation of enteric viruses in WSPs, (2) singlet oxygen is the ROS that mediates the indirect mechanism, and (3) the rate of inactivation by the indirect mechanism is proportional to the steady-state 1O2 concentration.

the inactivation of a model virus in water by a mechanism that may be relevant to the destruction of natural enteric viruses in surface waters.
the inactivation of enteric viruses, which is important to the safety of recreational waters and shellfish beds.
the indirect inactivation of MS 2 by sunlight in natural waters.
